**Commentary of Ibn ʿAṭiyya (al-Muḥarrar al-Wajīz) on Surah 38, verses 75–81:**

The Exalted and Majestic One said:

﴿He said, "O Iblīs, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?"﴾ ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ ﴿He said, "Then get out of it, for you are accursed."﴾ ﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense.﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are resurrected."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are among those reprieved"﴾ ﴿until the day of the appointed time.﴾

The one who speaks to Iblīs is Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. His words, ﴿What prevented you﴾, are a confirmation and a rebuke. ʿĀṣim and al-Jaḥdarī read "lammā khalaqtu" with a fatḥah on the lām of (lammā) and a shaddah on the mīm. The majority of people read ﴿"bi-yadayya"﴾ in the dual, and a group read "bi-yadiya" with a fatḥah on the yāʾ. In the Book of Allah the plural also occurs: ﴿with what Our hands have done﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 71]. All of these are expressions for power and might. This meaning was expressed by mentioning the hand in order to bring it closer to the listeners, since it is customary among humans that power, force and capability are exercised through the hand. The ignorance of the Arabs concerning Allah, the Exalted, required that their souls deny that creation could occur without direct contact, and similar rationally conceived meanings.

Al-Qāḍī Ibn al-Ṭayyib held that the hand, the eye and the face are attributes of essence (ṣifāt dhāt), additional to power, knowledge and the other well-established attributes of Allah, the Exalted. That view is rejected, and these are called the "informative attributes" (al-ṣifāt al-khabariyya). It is related in some reports that Allah, the Exalted, created four things with His own hand: the Throne, the Pen, the Garden of Eden, and Adam, while all other creatures He created by His word "Be." If this report is authentic, it was mentioned to honour these four and to draw attention to them. Otherwise, upon careful examination, every created thing comes into being through the power by which existence occurs after non-existence.

A group read ﴿"istakbarta"﴾ with a connecting alif, as a statement about Iblīs, and in that case "am" (or) is taken as an interruption (intiʿāf), not as an equivalent (muʿādila) to anything. Another group read "astakbarta" with a cut alif, as a question, and in this reading "am" is equivalent to the alif of interrogation. Many grammarians held that "am" does not serve as an equivalent to the alif when the two verbs differ, and that it is an equivalent only when both particles are attached to a single verb, as in your saying: "Did Zayd stand, or ʿAmr?" They said: when the two verbs differ, as in this verse, "am" is not an equivalent. The meaning of the verse is: "Has arrogance come upon you just now, or were you formerly among those who should not be required to do such a thing, given the loftiness of your station?" This is meant as a rebuke.

Iblīs's statement ﴿I am better than him﴾ is an analogy (qiyās) in which he erred. He thought that fire is superior to clay, and so he reasoned that what is created from the superior is itself superior to what is created from the inferior. He did not realise that virtues are specific designations from Allah, the Exalted, who marks with them whomever He wills. His statement contains a rejection of the wisdom of Allah, the Exalted, and an accusation of injustice against Him. This is clear from His words: ﴿Have you seen this one whom You have honoured?﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 62], and then he said: ﴿I am better than him.﴾ At this statement Iblīs's disbelief became joined to it, either out of obstinacy (ʿinād), according to those who permit that, or because knowledge was taken from him. Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 38, verses 82–88:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿He said: "Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all,﴾ ﴿except Your sincere servants among them."﴾ ﴿He said: "Then the truth, and the truth I speak:﴾ ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and those among them who follow you, all together."﴾ ﴿Say: "I do not ask of you any wage for it, nor am I of those who pretend.﴾ ﴿It is only a reminder to the worlds.﴾ ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time."﴾

The speaker is Iblis (Satan). He swore by the might of Allah, Exalted is He. Qatadah said: "The enemy of Allah knew that he had no might, so he swore by the might of Allah that he would mislead all of the descendants of Adam, except those whom Allah has purified for faith in Him."

The Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

This is an exception of the few from the many, within the scope of exception (istithna'), because the believers are far fewer than the disbelievers, as evidenced by the hadith of the sending forth of the Fire and other reports. Some scholars permitted that the many be excepted from the whole and the few be left under the original ruling, and they cited His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants, over them you have no authority, except for those who follow you of the misguided﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. Those who opposed them said: the word "servants" here includes humans and angels, so the exception remains within its normal scope, in that the few is what is excepted. The vowelling of the lam and its kasra in "al-mukhlisin" has already been discussed.

The speaker of ﴿Then the truth, and the truth I speak﴾ is Allah, Exalted is He. Mujahid said: the meaning is: "Then the truth is I." The majority (al-Jumhur) read both words in the accusative (naṣb). The second is in the accusative governed by "uqūlu" (I speak). As for the first, it may be an incitement (al-ighra'), or an oath with the particle of oath dropped, as if he said: "fa-wa al-haqqi" (by the truth), then the particle was elided, as you say: "Allahi la-af'alanna" (by Allah, I will surely do it), meaning "wa-Allahi." This is strengthened by His saying "la-amla'anna". Sibawayh said: I said to al-Khalil: what is the meaning of "la-af'alanna" when it comes at the beginning? He said: it is by the implied presence of an unexpressed oath. Another group said: the first is in the accusative governed by an implied verb.

Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid read both words in the nominative (raf'). As for the first, it is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is in His saying "la-amla'anna", because the meaning is: "That I will fill." As for the second, it is also in the nominative as a subject. 'Asim and Hamzah read the first in the nominative, which is the reading of Mujahid, al-A'mash, and Aban ibn Taghlib, and its grammar is clear. al-Hasan read "fa-al-haqqi wa-al-haqqi" with the qaf in the genitive (khafd), by way of oath, and Abu 'Amr al-Dani mentioned it.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform them that he does not ask for a wage or property, and that he is not one of those who pretend (yatakallafu) to what has not been entrusted to him, nor adorns himself with what he is not. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this verse abrogates His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "I do not ask of you any reward for it, except affection among relatives."﴾ [al-Shura: 23]. Al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The caller of the Prophet ﷺ called out: 'O Allah, forgive those who do not claim and do not pretend. Indeed I am free of pretension, and the righteous of my ummah.'"

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is only a reminder to the worlds﴾ means by it the Qur'an, and ﴿only a reminder﴾ means: a remembrance. Then Allah, Exalted is He, threatened them with His saying: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾, and this is by an elision, its estimate being: "And you will surely know the truth of its news after a time of your threat."

The people differed regarding the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿after a time﴾, to what time it refers. For "al-hin" in the language applies to a little or a long portion of time. Ibn Zayd said: it refers to the Day of Resurrection. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: it refers to the appointed terms (al-ajal) that are theirs, because each of them will know the realities after his death. al-Suddi said: it refers to the Day of Badr, because it is a day on which the disbelievers recognized the truth of the Qur'an's warning to them.

The commentary on Surah Sad is complete, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
